clue.text: Declined leadership for sport that has ups and downs

definitions.text: sport that has ups and downs

parts.note: fell means dropped or declined
running a firm is leading it, so running stands for leadership

explanation.surface: Someone stepped down from the captaincy of a sport whose fortunes go up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ups and downs' reads as changing fortunes but is literal: the sport is racing over hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing on foot over hilly, mountainous terrain literally involves climbing and descending.

clue.text: Award under nobleman's low part of organ

indicators.note: in a down clue the award is written below the nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An honour sits beneath a lord's rather lowly pipe organ part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a church instrument; it is the ear, and its lowest part.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fleshy lobe hangs at the bottom of the outer hearing organ.

clue.text: Both hands on top of car

parts.note: left and right hands are L and R, so both of them are L and R
over means above, on top of

explanation.surface: Someone keeps both hands on the car's roof.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a British make of four-wheel-drive off-road vehicle.

clue.text: Munch nuts without coatings, as originally intended

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters, as nuts lose their shells

explanation.surface: Eat shelled nuts the way nature meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shown in full, with no edits, is in the director's intended version.

clue.text: Knotted line around tangled nets

indicators.note: the letters are twisted into a new order, like knotted string

explanation.surface: A fishing line wound around snarled netting ends up knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a positional instruction but is anagram fodder; 'nets' links, meaning the wordplay gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nodular is covered with small lumps or knobs, like knots in wood.

clue.text: Good person, one with money, set up suckers

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ST is saint, a good person
I is the Roman numeral one
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A kind, wealthy person was framed by con artists.
explanation.walkthrough: STIWTIN is read upwards by 'set up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fools who are easily taken in are gullible dupes.

clue.text: Vaults rope to grab feline that's tame

parts.note: vaults are arched roofs, domes

indicators.note: the rope word grabs, holding the feline in its middle

parts.note: to rope is to tie
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: Someone leaps over a rope to catch a docile cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaults' suggests leaping, but it is the noun: arched ceilings.
explanation.definitionFit: Here tame is a verb: to train a wild animal to live with humans.

clue.text: A group of volunteers supporting leg that's broken at party

indicators.note: in a down clue, the leg sits below and holds up the rest

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers prop up someone whose leg was broken at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' looks like part of the injury, but it describes the answer being smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorated container full of sweets is smashed open with sticks at children's celebrations.

clue.text: Letter about computer parts

indicators.note: the computer word parts, or splits apart, the word for about, sitting between its two letters

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds
a micro is a microcomputer

explanation.surface: A letter written concerning components of a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun after 'computer', but it is a verb: MICRO separates O from N.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fifteenth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Pupils dance at the sides in musical

indicators.note: the edge letters of dance are placed inside the musical's name

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of the word dance are taken, its two sides

explanation.surface: Students dance along the edges of the stage in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainees at a military or police academy are students learning a profession.

clue.text: Careless in approach, hiding errata regularly

indicators.note: the coming word hides the picked letters inside it

parts.note: an advent is a coming, an approach

indicators.note: every other letter of errata is taken, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Mistakes were concealed carelessly in the approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks ERT from 'errata'; ADVENT hides it as ADV-ERT-ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An unintentional, accidental act is done without due care.

clue.text: Recalled old chap in French street displaying charm

indicators.note: called back, so the whole assembly is read from the end to the start
the old chap sits inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Someone remembered an elderly gentleman in a Parisian street who was full of charm.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE with OMAN inside gives RUOMANE, which 'Recalled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate someone or make them fall in love is to charm them.

clue.text: Sound eager to hear story-teller

indicators.note: the words are judged by how they come across when heard, not how they are written

parts.note: to toll is to sound, as a bell does, and keen means eager

explanation.surface: A healthy person keen to listen to a raconteur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy, but it is a verb meaning ring a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings was a celebrated writer of tales.

clue.text: One in hurl of abuse leaving job

indicators.note: the letter for one departs from inside the outburst

parts.note: a tirade is a long outburst of abuse
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone quits their post amid a torrent of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled occupation such as plumbing is a craft or line of work.

clue.text: Sprayed liquid provides covering over area

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the letter for area
liquid means fluid, flowing, so the letters of provides flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A sprayed fluid provides a protective coating across a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' is the anagram signal for 'provides', giving VPORISED; A goes in after the V.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid turned into a fine mist or vapour, as from an aerosol, has been atomised.

clue.text: Dislike interrupting a host

indicators.note: the dislike word breaks into the middle of the word for a

parts.note: per means a, as in once a day
to resent is to dislike

explanation.surface: Someone's hostility disrupts a person hosting an event.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who introduces a television show or compères an event is its anchor.

clue.text: Head of construction following schedule to make part of airport

indicators.note: only the leading letter of construction is used

parts.note: a project following its schedule is on course

explanation.surface: A building foreman sticks to the timetable to complete a section of an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: The large open hall of a terminal where passengers gather is the central concourse area.

clue.text: Finally, Amazon Echo working with bit one's recently delivered

indicators.note: only the last letter of Amazon is used

parts.note: Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet
on means working, operating
bit, chewed into, is taken as ate, consumed

explanation.surface: An Amazon Echo smart speaker arrived just now with a part attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a package delivered by Amazon; the delivery is a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn baby is one that has very recently been born.

clue.text: Dark brown sauce fantastic, rejecting wan rubbish

indicators.note: the leftover letters are fantastically rearranged
the letters of wan are thrown out
the letters of wan go in any order, as rubbish is jumbled

explanation.surface: A brown sauce is so good it puts pale rubbish to shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Take W, A, N out of BROWNSAUCE and rearrange BROSUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something murky, dim and hard to see is gloomy, lacking light.

clue.text: Close to Dallas, dig biker's bar

indicators.note: the close, or end, of Dallas gives its final letter

parts.note: a dig is a poke, a jab

explanation.surface: Near Dallas, someone digs at a motorcyclists' pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biker's bar' suggests a drinking place, but it is a rod in a bicycle wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist's wheel has radiating rods connecting hub and rim.

clue.text: Following opponents, gun raised on sudden attack

indicators.note: the raised gun comes after the opponents

parts.note: in bridge, South and East sit on opposing sides

indicators.note: in a down clue the gun word is read upwards

parts.note: an Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: After the enemy lifted their weapons, a surprise assault followed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit or stroke strikes abruptly, as does a convulsion.

clue.text: Exposed valley with river running north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A valley was revealed, with a river flowing northwards through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncovered or laid bare has been revealed.

clue.text: Appropriate route's organised with run

indicators.note: the letters of route's are arranged into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A suitable path has been planned out, complete with a running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective, but here it is a verb meaning take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket money, often dishonestly, is to take it for one's own use.

clue.text: European in company of others adjusted once more

indicators.note: the European sits among the others, inside them

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A European in a group of others made another adjustment.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or bone set again has been put right a second time.

clue.text: Noted tunnel within hospital department

indicators.note: the tunnel sits inside the department's letters

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat
a mine is a tunnel dug underground

explanation.surface: A passage was observed running inside part of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distinguished and famous in their field is well known.

clue.text: Random tripe removed from otherwise superlative prizes

indicators.note: the letters of tripe are taken in any order
those letters are taken out of the longer word
the remaining letters are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Pointless nonsense was cut from an otherwise outstanding set of awards.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, R, I, P, E from SUPERLATIVE and rearrange the leftover SULAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Here prizes is a verb: to treasure or hold something dear.

clue.text: A river crossed by brown bovine

indicators.note: the brown word runs across, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: tan is a light brown
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A stream crossed by a brown cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac, so this adjective means bull-like.

clue.text: Clerical buildings housing fine English dining rooms

indicators.note: the clerical buildings take in the other letters

parts.note: rectories are the houses of rectors, Anglican clergy
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Church houses contain fine English dining rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Monasteries and colleges have communal halls where meals are eaten.
